name: Treaty with the Kickapoo of the Vermilion, 1819 (Treaty of Fort Harrison)
nations: Kickapoo of the Vermilion (successors: Kickapoo Tribe in Kansas, Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma)
promises: Articles 1 and 2: the Kickapoo of the Vermilion ceded all their lands on the Wabash and its waters, within bounds from the Vincennes tract to the Vermilion River and Pine Creek.

Article 3: they gave up their existing $1,000 annuity; the United States would pay $2,000 a year in specie for ten years, which with $3,000 then delivered was to be full compensation for the cession and all their treaty claims.
Article 4: the annuity to be paid where later agreed, since the tribe contemplated removing.

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission treated this treaty and the Kickapoo treaty of July 30, 1819 together as the Kickapoo cession of Royce Area 110, valued the Kickapoo interest at $11,833,330 against net consideration of $406,200 (which counts this treaty's $2,000 annuity for ten years and cash), found the consideration unconscionable, and awarded $11,427,130 subject to offsets.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Kickapoo Tribe of Kansas et al. v. United States, Docket 315 (consolidated with Docket 15-D and others), Findings 75, 87 and 88 and Order of August 25, 1978 (42 Ind. Cl. Comm. 354)

source.title: Pottawatomie Tribe et al. v. United States, Findings of Fact on Value and Consideration, Part 2 (August 25, 1978)
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Library, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

landTaken: Part of Royce Area 110 in Illinois and Indiana; the Commission valued the Kickapoo interest in the whole of Area 110 ceded by the two 1819 treaties and did not state a separate acreage for this treaty.
compensation: The Commission credited $426,700 in gross consideration under both 1819 treaties, less $20,500 for the annuities the Kickapoo released, leaving $406,200. The award of $11,427,130 was subject to offsets. On September 29, 1978 the case was certified and transferred to the United States Court of Claims.
today: The same award is recorded for the July 30, 1819 treaty (kappler-190); it is one award for the two treaties and should not be counted twice. The final outcome in the Court of Claims was not traced in this pass.

plain.promised: The Kickapoo of the Vermilion gave up their Wabash lands and a $1,000 annuity for $2,000 a year for ten years and $3,000 in hand, called full compensation.
plain.happened: In 1978 the Indian Claims Commission valued the Kickapoo cession under this and the July 1819 treaty at $11,833,330, found the $406,200 paid unconscionable, and awarded $11,427,130 subject to offsets.
plain.today: The case was transferred to the Court of Claims in 1978; the final outcome has not been traced. The award is shared with the July 1819 Kickapoo treaty.

openQuestions: The Commission's Part 1 opinion says this treaty was ratified on May 10, 1820 but takes January 13, 1821, the ratification of the amended July 30, 1819 treaty, as the valuation date for both.
Findings Part 2 cites this treaty as '78 Stat. 202', a scan or typing error for 7 Stat. 202.
The Court of Claims outcome after the 1978 transfer was not found here; kappler-190 notes search results pointing to a January 5, 1979 judgment for $11,427,130 that could not be loaded.
No Kickapoo Tribe in Kansas or Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma account of this treaty was found.
